headline: Calpine deal transforms scale; margins widen, debt climbs
summary_short: Constellation reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $11,122M, up 63.8% y/y, and diluted EPS of $4.49, up from $0.38 a year ago, as the January 2026 Calpine acquisition added consolidated scale and a $721M favorable swing in unrealized hedge fair-value adjustments boosted GAAP earnings.
summary_long: Revenue rose to $11,122M (+63.8% y/y), driven mainly by consolidating Calpine (acquired January 7, 2026, ~$21.8B). GAAP net income was $1,590M ($4.49 diluted EPS) vs. $118M ($0.38) a year ago; Adjusted (non-GAAP) Operating Earnings were $972M ($2.74/share) vs. $673M ($2.14/share). The GAAP swing also reflects a $721M favorable unrealized hedge fair-value gain and a $174M favorable nuclear ARO remeasurement, partly offset by $119M of Calpine merger/integration costs and unfavorable nuclear-outage impacts. Cash fell to $800M (-56.7% y/y) after acquisition-related investing outflows; long-term debt rose to $16,994M as CEG assumed Calpine's debt. The board declared a $0.4265/share quarterly dividend; no buybacks occurred this quarter. No guidance was reiterated in this filing.

drivers.explanation: Growth reflects the January 2026 Calpine consolidation plus higher capacity revenues, partly offset by weather-driven cost increases and lower CMC program revenue.
Company cites the Calpine addition, favorable unrealized hedge gains, a favorable nuclear ARO remeasurement, and higher capacity revenues, partly offset by unfavorable nuclear outages.
Margin expansion is arithmetically explained by operating income growing faster than revenue post-Calpine consolidation; the filing does not separately decompose margin drivers.
Debt rose as Constellation assumed Calpine's outstanding long-term debt and issued new debt to help fund the acquisition.
Cash fell mainly due to cash consideration paid for the Calpine acquisition and related investing outflows.
Management attributes the earnings swing primarily to the Calpine acquisition and favorable hedge/decommissioning fair-value moves, offset by merger/integration costs and nuclear outages.
